references.text: The original instruction from God to Moses to build the bronze altar of acacia wood, with the same dimensions: five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high.
The bronze altar is mentioned as part of the equipment to be made for the tabernacle.
Moses was instructed to place the bronze altar in front of the entrance to the tabernacle.
Moses placed the bronze altar at the entrance to the tabernacle and offered burnt offerings and grain offerings on it.
The bronze altar is used to offer burnt offerings to the Lord, as a pleasing aroma.
Solomon built a bronze altar that was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high—a much larger altar for the temple.
Ezekiel's vision of the dimensions of the future altar, showing continuity in the significance of the altar in God's worship.
The author of Hebrews mentions that we have an altar from which those who serve in the tabernacle have no right to eat—pointing to Christ as our final sacrifice.
Direct link between God's command (Ex 27) and its actual execution (Ex 38), confirming the importance of obedience.
Complementary description of the same object: 38:1 gives dimensions and form, while 38:7 explains the transport mechanism.
